verdict_detail: At fixed v*=e^2/2, mixture weights of low-d families are substantially more identifiable from Z samples than from raw magnitude samples of equal size. Binary prime-mass MAE ratio n_mle/z_mle ~10.7 (M>=250); Fisher I_Z/I_n ~90-240. Mechanism: parking Z=1 is Bernoulli-equivalent to primality under exact Z at v*. Qualification: model-free park is unique to v*; log-Z MLE works for a band of large v; multi-family simplex advantage is real but uneven (mean L1 ratio ~3.6).

attacks.name: just_p_vs_np_with_labels
attacks.argument: If you already have d(n) or primality labels, π is the empirical frequency; Z is unnecessary.
attacks.response: Path B assumes unlabeled observations of the process output (Z or n). Labels are not available to either observer.

attacks.name: computing_Z_needs_d_n
attacks.argument: Z requires d(n), so any advantage is circular for cryptographic scales.
attacks.response: Claim is about sample complexity of π given already-observed Z vs observed n magnitudes, not computational primality.

attacks.name: wrong_v_destroys_parking
attacks.argument: Advantage is knife-edge at v* only.
attacks.response: v-sensitivity table measures this; survivor requires peak near v*.

attacks.name: raw_n_with_modular_features_enough
